hero.sub: AI is useful when it changes how the business operates. We find the work where AI can remove manual effort, shorten cycle times or create capacity, then help turn the opportunity into something people can actually use.

sections.heading: How Commview Thinks About AI in Business
intro: AI is not a strategy in itself. It is another way to change how work gets done.

That means we do not start with a model, platform or list of fashionable use cases. We start with the operation. Where is time being lost? Which work repeats? Where are people moving information between systems? Where does slow access to information hold up a decision?
If AI can materially improve the way that work happens, it has a job to do. If a simpler process change, automation or existing tool solves the problem better, we use that instead.
The point is not to add more AI. The point is to make the business work better.

sections.heading: Where AI Actually Earns Its Place in B2B Operations
sections.intro: The useful opportunities tend to sit inside work that is repetitive, information-heavy or slowed down by manual hand-offs. These are five areas we look at first.

items.title: Reporting and analysis
items.body: Reduce the manual work involved in collecting, structuring and summarising information so people spend more time interpreting what changed and what to do next.

items.title: Workflow automation
items.body: Connect repeatable steps across systems, trigger the next action and keep people involved where judgement, approval or exception handling matters.

items.title: Content and translation
items.body: Use AI to accelerate drafting, adaptation, summarisation and translation while keeping human review around accuracy, brand and commercial judgement.

items.title: Lead scoring and routing
items.body: Bring behavioural and account signals together to help prioritise attention and route opportunities without pretending a score can replace commercial judgement.

items.title: Sales intelligence
items.body: Turn fragmented customer and account information into useful context for preparation, follow-up and decision support without adding another manual research task.

sections.heading: Do Not Start With AI. Start With the Work.
sections.intro: A useful AI initiative should have a clear operational reason to exist. We keep the path deliberately practical.

steps.title: Find the friction
steps.body: Identify repetitive work, delays, manual hand-offs and information bottlenecks.

steps.title: Understand the workflow
steps.body: Map what happens today, who is involved, which systems matter and where judgement is required.

steps.title: Choose the intervention
steps.body: Decide whether AI, conventional automation, process change or a combination is the sensible answer.

steps.title: Build small
steps.body: Create the smallest useful implementation that can prove whether the idea works in the real operation.

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: Look at adoption and the operational change, including time, cost, capacity, quality or cycle time where measurable.

steps.title: Scale what works
steps.body: Expand only when the evidence supports it, with controls and human oversight appropriate to the workflow.

sections.eyebrow: A DIFFERENT KIND OF AI CONSULTING
sections.heading: Where Commview Is Different From the Big Consultancies
sections.intro: A scale-up usually does not need a transformation programme before it can improve the way work gets done. The engagement should be proportionate to the problem.

columns.title: Traditional consultancy model
items: Strategy can be separated from implementation

columns.title: Commview
items: Start with a specific operational constraint
Build, test and measure before scaling

heading: Automate the work.
Not the accountability.
body: AI can draft, classify, summarise, extract, route and recommend. That does not mean every decision should be delegated to it.

We design around the consequence of being wrong. Where a workflow affects customers, money, compliance, reputation or an important commercial decision, the right controls and human review need to stay visible.
The objective is useful leverage, not autonomy for its own sake.

sections.heading: Judge AI by What Changes in the Operation
intro: A successful implementation is not one that produces the most impressive demo. It is one that becomes useful enough to change the way work happens.
We look for measurable operational evidence: less manual work, shorter cycle times, more capacity, fewer avoidable hand-offs, better access to information or a more consistent process.
Where we publish AI work, the case study will show the problem, what changed and the outcome rather than treating the technology itself as the result.

items.a: AI consulting helps a business identify where artificial intelligence can create useful operational or commercial change, then plan and implement it. For Commview, that starts with the work rather than the technology. We examine the workflow, the problem, the available data and the consequence of errors before deciding whether AI belongs in the solution.

items.q: How much does AI consulting cost?
items.a: AI consulting costs depend on the scope of the problem, the systems involved and whether the work covers diagnosis, implementation or a broader operating change. Commview does not publish a fixed price because a focused workflow project and a cross-functional transformation are materially different engagements. We scope the work around the outcome required.

items.q: What is the difference between AI consulting and an AI agency?
items.a: The labels overlap, so the practical difference is usually the work being bought. An AI agency may focus on building a particular automation, agent or technical solution. AI consulting can start earlier by deciding where AI is worth using, redesigning the workflow and connecting implementation to the wider operating and commercial context.

items.q: Can AI actually reduce our costs?
items.a: AI can reduce costs when it removes enough repetitive work, delay or manual processing to justify the implementation and ongoing operating cost. It does not automatically make a process cheaper. The business case should compare the current workflow with the proposed one and measure what changes after deployment.

items.q: Do we need an AI strategy before we start?
items.a: Not always. A B2B scale-up can often start with a specific operational problem, test a useful intervention and learn from it before creating a wider AI programme. A broader strategy becomes more valuable when multiple teams, systems, governance requirements and investment decisions need to be coordinated.

items.q: How do you decide which AI use case to tackle first?
items.a: Start with the work that creates meaningful friction and can be measured. We look at frequency, time consumed, process complexity, available information, error consequences and the value of improving the workflow. The first use case should be useful enough to matter but contained enough to test without creating unnecessary transformation risk.

sections.heading: Find the work where AI can actually earn its place.
